haiku-low.q1: A PR builds the image without pushing and runs make test-unit; results go on the PR, nothing deploys. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production deploy the same image, tagged with the merge commit SHA. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration failure gets one retry; if it fails twice, the run ends and unit tests are cancelled if running. Unit failure gets no retry; the run ends and integration is cancelled if running.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs previous_tag. deploy.sh rollback staging sets the image and current_tag back to previous_tag, which is read from SSM.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers may approve, not the merge commit author. If no one approves within 72 hours, the run expires, nothing reaches production, and it is posted.
haiku-low.q6: In AWS SSM Parameter Store: current_tag and previous_tag per environment. deploy.sh writes them only after a rollout succeeds; the canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Stable is unchanged, SSM tags are unchanged, and canary-off removes the canary. The schema change stays applied, since migrations are forward-only with no undo.
haiku-low.q8: The older run is cancelled as superseded if it has not started its canary, and nothing is posted. A run already in canary or production finishes.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window it waits holding no lock until the next window. If production-deploy is held, it waits; it is cancelled only if a newer run takes staging-deploy.
haiku-low.q10: The canary 5xx ratio over the last minute, checked by the run every 30 seconds from minute 1 to 15. Failure: above 1%, no data, or query error; then canary-off.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED for how approvers are notified. The manual approval job is restricted to release-approvers. The information shown to approvers is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: Before tags are written, kubectl rollout undo returns to the running tag, since current_tag names it. After tags are written, deploy.sh rollback is used, because it goes to previous_tag.

sonnet.q1: A PR builds the image without pushing it and runs `make test-unit`; results appear on the PR and nothing is deployed. A merge to `main` starts a run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the one image built from the merge commit, tagged with the full SHA at registry.internal/shop-api. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration tests get one automatic retry (two attempts at most); if they fail after the retry, the run ends, unit tests are cancelled if still running, and it is posted to #deploys. Unit tests get no retry. A failure ends the run, cancels integration if still running, and is posted to #deploys.
sonnet.q4: Staging runs `previous_tag`, the build it ran before. `deploy.sh rollback staging` reads `previous_tag` from SSM, sets the image back to it and writes `current_tag` back to it. The run ends and is posted. If rollback fails, the run goes to HOLD.
sonnet.q5: Members of the `release-approvers` CI group, but not the author of the merge commit. If no one answers within 72 hours, the run expires, nothing goes to production, and it is posted to #deploys.
sonnet.q6: In SSM Parameter Store, as `current_tag` and `previous_tag` per environment. `deploy.sh` writes them only after a rollout succeeds. The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: Stable is unchanged. The canary is removed with `deploy.sh canary-off` and the run ends. The tags are not written. The schema keeps any migration already applied, because migrations are forward-only and cannot be undone. Each migration still works with the previous image.
sonnet.q8: The older run is cancelled as superseded, as long as it has not started its canary. This covers waiting for approval, the window or `production-deploy`. Nothing is posted to #deploys.
sonnet.q9: Outside the window, it waits with no lock held and no time limit, until the next window. It stays valid until it is superseded. If another production deploy is in progress, it waits for the `production-deploy` lock and is not failed. It is cancelled only if a newer run takes `staging-deploy`.
sonnet.q10: The canary 5xx ratio is measured: 5xx requests over all requests for app shop-api-canary, over the last minute. The run queries Prometheus every 30 seconds for 15 minutes, from minute 1 to minute 15. A check fails if the ratio is above 1%, if there is no data, or if the query errors. A failed check runs `canary-off` and ends the run.
sonnet.q12: Staging: if the rollout fails, run `kubectl rollout undo` on staging. Production: run `kubectl rollout undo` on production, then `deploy.sh canary-off`. The tags were not written, so `current_tag` still names the running tag, and undo returns to it. `deploy.sh rollback` would go to `previous_tag`, one step too far back. If undo fails, the run goes to HOLD.
